note:
CORRECTION TO MY OWN OPERATOR NOTE OF AN HOUR AGO. I proposed this before draining:

    pgrep -f "[s]luice-run.sh" >/dev/null && echo "busy" || bash scripts/sluice-drain.sh N

IT CANNOT SEE A CENSUS. A census job is `sluice-census.sh` -> `census-run.sh`; it never spawns sluice-run.sh, and sluice-run.sh REFUSES `census` as a phase on purpose (census-run.sh takes the shared claim itself and deletes the claim file on exit, so nesting it would clobber the outer job's claim). So the pattern returns nothing while the box is fully occupied, and I used it tonight to conclude "idle" while campaign/the-murrain's census held the staff — then launched a drain that claimed the next row and sat blocked behind it.

Same error class as the empty ~/.bash_history I nearly reported as evidence earlier: a check with no power to find its target reads exactly like a check that found nothing.

THE CORRECT CHECK IS THE ONE THE PROJECT ALREADY HAS, and it is authoritative because it asks about the CLAIM rather than about any particular script:

    bash scripts/census-run.sh status

    census running: pid 1365907 (nathan@lefford) since 2026-09-07T22:51:48Z,
      writing .../hornvale-census-wt/book/src/laboratory/generated,
      running census-run @ @85ef1edd3

It names the holder whichever script took it — chamber, census or heavy — because all three take the same shared flock (0081/0086/0133). That is the whole point of there being one claim.

So the discipline is:

    bash scripts/census-run.sh status >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "busy" || bash scripts/sluice-drain.sh N

and NOT a pgrep for any one script's name. A process-name check has to enumerate every script that can hold the box; the claim check asks the box itself.

The stacked-drain consequence is unchanged and still small: a blocked chamber process holds a row reading `running` while executing nothing. Nothing is corrupted; the flock serialises. But my remedy was broken in exactly the way the original note was written to prevent.
